title: An Unexpected Coupling Reaction of 8-Quinolinolate at Elevated Temperature

synthesis.procedure: Method i: 8-hydroxyquinoline (0.29 g, 2.00 mmol), SmCo (0.77 g, 1.73 mmol), 1,3,5-tri-tert-butylbenzene (0.15 g, 0.61 mmol), and two drops of mercury were placed in a thick-walled glass tube under N2 (glovebox). The tube was evacuated, sealed, and heated at 210 °C for 7 days then 130 °C for 3 days. The tube was opened under N2, the contents transferred to a Schlenk flask, and dry acetonitrile (100 mL) added. The mixture was heated at 70 °C for 30 min, cooled, and filtered. Residual SmCo was removed magnetically and remaining 8-hydroxyquinoline was washed out with hexane. The solid was dried under vacuum; red crystals of 1 were identified among a red–brown powder by unit-cell comparison with known [LaNi2(OQ)7] and [LaCo2(OQ)7]. Crystals were of insufficient quality for a full data collection. Bulk characterisation was not possible because of extremely low isolable yields. CAUTION: reactions produce H2 in sealed tubes.
synthesis.temperature: 210 °C for 7 days then 130 °C for 3 days; acetonitrile workup at 70 °C
synthesis.vessel_or_method: evacuated sealed thick-walled glass tube; furnace; glovebox/Schlenk workup
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: Opened under N2; partial dissolution in dry MeCN (100 mL) at 70 °C, cool, filter; magnetic removal of residual SmCo; hexane wash of residual HOQ; vacuum drying; red crystals of 1 identified microscopically.
synthesis.yield: extremely low (isolable crystals; bulk characterisation impossible)

source_locations.location: Experimental, Method i; Results and Discussion

synthesis.procedure: Method iii: 8-hydroxyquinoline (0.30 g, 2.07 mmol), SmCo (0.77 g, 1.74 mmol), 1,2,4,5-tetramethylbenzene (1.50 g, 11.2 mmol), and six drops of mercury were placed in a thick-walled glass tube under N2. The tube was evacuated, sealed, and heated at 200 °C for 7 days. Small yellow crystals of [Sm3(OQ)5(BQ)2(H2O)] (3Sm) were manually separated from crude solid including a red glass. Repeating the reaction at 270 °C for 7 days gave crystals with the same unit cell. Products after separation from residual metal, flux, and red glass were air-stable. The red glass contained Sm, Co, and Hg by EDX. Bulk characterisation was impossible because of extremely low isolable yields.
synthesis.vessel_or_method: evacuated sealed thick-walled glass tube; furnace; glovebox manipulations
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: Small yellow crystals hand-picked with an oil-coated spatula from crude solid/red glass.

source_locations.location: Abstract; Experimental, Method iii; Crystal data for 3Sm

synthesis.procedure: Method iv: 8-hydroxyquinoline (0.30 g, 2.07 mmol), Er filings (0.09 g, 0.52 mmol), nickel powder (0.03 g, 0.51 mmol), 1,2,4,5-tetramethylbenzene (1.00 g, 7.45 mmol), and two drops of mercury were placed in a thick-walled glass tube under N2. The tube was evacuated, sealed, and heated at 260 °C for 7 days. Yellow crystals of 3Er were isolated in low yield (~1%). Identity was confirmed by unit-cell comparison with 3Sm; crystals were of insufficient quality for a full data collection.
